The FY 10-K lands with or immediately after this print; the covenant schedule and the auditor's language are the highest-variance items and they sit in the last 10-Q's liquidity section, recoverable today.

Check EDGAR 8-Ks filed in the last two weeks, any lender amendment, and any Nasdaq listing-qualification correspondence — at $0.5951 a minimum-bid-price deficiency notice is live and a reverse-split proposal could be announced alongside results.

The brand-divestiture programme: proceeds, gains/losses, and impairment of remaining intangibles. Hain has been selling brands; the carrying value of what is left against a $58m market cap versus the debt stack is where the equity value actually gets decided.
FY2027 guidance existence, not level — whether management guides at all is the binary this print turns on given one analyst estimate.
Consensus is one estimate (-$0.03). Do not treat it as an anchor; there is effectively no sell-side surface to be surprised against.

names.session_evidence: Release states results published before market open on 2026-09-14 with a live call at 1:30 p.m. BST / 8:30 a.m. ET — https://investor.coinshares.com/pressreleases/coinshares-announces-date-of-first-half-2026-financial-results. bmo is company-stated, not calendar-inferred.
names.why_history_untrustworthy: The baseline's three 'moves' are 6-K text matches, and the 6-K trail on CIK 0002087587 contains only three 6-Ks (2026-04-22, 2026-05-01, 2026-08-24). The 2026-08-24 one is verified as a NOTICE OF EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002087587/000121390026092804/ea0303148-6k_coinshares.htm), not an earnings release. The inferred 62-day cadence the baseline itself calls implausible is an artefact of matching corporate-action 6-Ks. There is NO usable US earnings reaction base rate for this name — n is effectively 0, not 3, and the 4.46% expected move and 2.23% deadband derived from those three are meaningless.
where_to_look: The gap between what was already reported to the Swedish market and what the SEC-format H1 release says. CoinShares has a European reporting history and a US one that starts now; any difference in presentation, segment split or reconciliation between the two is a genuine information event that no US analyst has a prior for.

CoinShares' own published research surface — the weekly/monthly Digital Asset Fund Flows and AUM reports at coinshares.com/insights/research-data. H1 average AUM and therefore the management-fee run-rate are substantially reconstructable from already-public data; the edge is in the lines that are not (principal investment P&L, hedge-fund segment, staking/lending income).

Balance-sheet principal holdings marked to market. The digital-asset price path over H1 2026 likely drives 'other income' more than the fee business does, and it is the line with the widest spread of plausible outcomes.

The 2026-09-15 EGM — the day AFTER the print. The proxy seeks approval of a 2026 Equity Incentive Plan with an 11% initial share pool plus 3% annual evergreen for 2027-2029 (https://investor.coinshares.com/pressreleases/notice-of-virtual-extraordinary-general-meeting-of-coinshares-plc-on-september-15-2026). Dilution of that size adjacent to a results release is an unusual configuration.
The 20-F filed 2026-04-30 and the 424B3/F-1: risk factors and accounting policy for digital assets, which set the shape of what the H1 numbers can look like.
Options chain is unusable (368 total OI, no two-sided ATM). There is no priced-move anchor here at all.

Find the cause: check EDGAR for 8-Ks, any ATM/shelf usage, any customer or contract loss, and any index/rebalance effect. A drawdown that size with a confirmed date already on the tape is the single most specific question on this name.

Customer concentration. Microlab and the DAC thermal-cooling line sell into a small number of wireless carrier and data-centre buyers; read the last 10-Q's concentration note, then read what those named customers have said about capex timing in their own recent disclosures. This is a one-or-two-customer business dressed as a component maker.
Backlog. RF Industries discloses a backlog number in its releases; the Q2 figure and the Q2 call's language about order timing set what the Q3 print has to beat.

The option chain reads 24.5% implied but carries 297 total OI and a 67%-of-mid ATM spread. Treat it as indicative only; the 9.27% historical median is the better anchor and the two disagree by a factor of 2.6.
Only two estimates ($0.18 consensus against $0.09 a year ago). A doubling is the implied bar and it rests on two analysts.

names.why_history_caveat: The baseline's n=0 is GENUINE ABSENCE, not a matcher failure. CODA's EDGAR trail shows it does not file 8-K item 2.02 for earnings at all — it issues a press release and files the 10-Q the same day (10-Qs on 2026-06-15, 2026-03-17, 2025-09-15; every 8-K in the last two years is item 5.02 or 5.07). So the matcher correctly found nothing and imported no wrong filings. The consequence is that there is no reaction base rate, no options market, and the 1.83% deadband rests on 20-day realised vol alone — a hunter must not read n=0 as 'quiet stock'.

The 8-K filed 2026-09-10, items 5.07 and 9.01, four days before the print, plus the DEF 14A (2026-08-17) and PRE 14A (2026-08-06). Something was put to shareholders immediately before results; read what the proposals were and how they voted.

Defence and subsea order flow. The Products segment (Echoscope/DAVD) sells to a handful of navies, port-security and offshore construction buyers; read the prior 10-Q's customer-concentration note and then look for the specific award announcements behind it. This is a lumpy-order business where one contract moves a quarter.
The Colmek/Services segment's contract timing, which is the offsetting swing factor against Products.

The Form S-3 shelf that went effective 2026-03-31 (424B3 2026-04-01): check whether anything has been drawn. A $111m company with a live shelf and 74k shares/day of volume has a financing trail worth tracing.
No options market and 74,343 shares/day average volume — whatever is found here, capacity is the binding constraint, well under the $200k turnover floor's comfort zone at ~$750k/day notional.

sweep_notes: Zero phantoms. All four dates came from a company press release or company IR page, not from a vendor calendar, and all four sessions came from a stated release time or call time rather than from the calendar's label.

One session was a genuine catch rather than a confirmation: RFIL's last seven prints were all amc by 8-K acceptance time and this one is company-stated bmo. The calendar was right, but only by accident of the company changing its practice.

Two baselines carry no usable earnings base rate. CSHR's three 'moves' are corporate-action 6-Ks (one verified as an EGM notice) and must not be inherited — baseline_history_trustworthy is false. CODA's n=0 is real absence because the company does not file item 2.02 8-Ks; the matcher was correct and imported nothing wrong, so the flag stays true, but the expected-move and deadband fields are unanchored for both names.

Three of four names have no usable options chain (CSHR, CODA, HAIN). Only RFIL has a quoted implied move and its ATM spread is 67% of mid, so the day has essentially no option-implied anchor anywhere.

Capacity: CODA ~$750k/day notional, CSHR ~$1.06m, RFIL ~$1.70m, HAIN ~$417k. Three of four are thin against the trading rule's $200k floor and none is comfortable above $5m turnover, so a large finding on this day may not be tradeable at size.
